answer: Entry wears a velvet glove: joining is cheap, but leaving takes a public cooling period, and any challenger who proves fakery claims the stake as bounty, so no botnet harvests and vanishes. Each identity carries an atlas, a map of past interactions; each epoch the network samples a random walk through it, and every claimed edge needs two independent witnesses staking their own standing, so fabricating N histories costs about N squared in bribes and burned witnesses. Influence is capped by a zenith that rises only with verified work, so a fresh fake starts at the floor and cannot buy altitude.
